   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Paul Rowland, CHESTER

Ron & Brian,

Has anyone ever compiled a list
of interfaces that will or will
not work with the Spectrum +2A &
+D?

I have the following interfaces
and I am unsure if I can use
them :- Cheetah sound sampler,
AMX mouse, DK'Tronics lightpen,
Cheetah Specdrum.

Hope you can help,

             Thanks.

          Paul Rowland

To Paul Rowland from Brian Gaff

A tricky one this, as the +2A is
not exactly compatible with the
+D anyway! I don't think you can
do any harm trying the devices
though.

It all depends what ports the
other interfaces use, how accur-
ately their internal decoding of
the address bus is and obviously
whether the software clashes.

There were several versions of
the DK'Tronics light pen,so this
may also make compiling a list a
bit difficult.The +D hates being
too far away from the Spectrum,
or having other devices with
internal ROMs on at the same
time.

If I had to gamble, I would say
the Cheetah devices are the most
likely to work, assuming they
run on the +2A. The light pen
may work, but I have no idea
about the mouse.

                         - B.G.

From Jim Hossack - WEST KILBRIDE

I wonder if you know where I can
get information on ROM routines
such as PRINT, LOAD, BEEP etc.
amd how to use them. I can't
remember noticing much along
those lines in any books I've
read about Spectrum machine
code. In the past, I have
encountered one or two useful
routines in "Outclass", but feel
it would be nice to have a full
list - assuming it's not a
jealously guarded Amstrad or MGT
trade secret! Is the position of
ROM calls essentially the same
with the 48k/+3/Sam/Opus or does
it depend on the machine? Many
thanks, keep up the Good Work,

                  - Jim Hossack

Brian Cavers to Jim Hossack

Beginning this very month in ADD
ENDERS is a brilliant new series
by Francis Miles. This is "THE
SPECTRUM ROM INDEX".It is a huge
reference work on the Spectrum
48K ROM and will take many
months to complete. It is meant,
ideally, to be used in conjunct-
ion with the book "THE COMPLETE
SPECTRUM ROM DISASSEMBLY"but you
may need to search your local
library for a copy or classified
adverts like MICRO MART.

However,some of the simpler uses
of ROM routines might be covered
by OUTCLASS. I'll ask Chris Pile
or Malcolm Goodman next time I
write.

48K ROM calls are the same on
any Spectrum but different for
SAM.
                        - Brian

From:Vincent L.Jacks, LONDON,SE9




Dear Ron & Brian,

Could you please help me out
with two problems I am having at
the moment. The two problems are
not related so I'll explain then
separately.

Firstly, I am getting bored with
the same old menu screens on all
my programs:mainly blank screen,
white text. I am in the process
of setting up some new menu
screens and as I only program in
BASIC, I'm fairly satisfied with
what I've come up with.

However, now to problem No 1. I
would like to set up a similar
bar menu system like that on the
Spectrum start up (The bar that
goes up and down). I've searched
all the libraries in my area to
try to find a book on this
particular subject; no luck I'm
afraid. I did learn that it has
something to do with the
Input/Output ports, (Namely IN
61438) and the up/down cursor
keys - CHR$ 10 and CHR$ 11.

Can you help as the little inf-
ormation that I've found doesn't
give me much to go on. How, for
instance, to use these and make
the bar menu system and
incorporate it into my own
program?

Machine Code always makes me ill
even if I look at it so can this
type of programming be done in
BASIC,despite its limitations?

Now to problem No 2. I recently
upgraded my DOS system to UNIDOS
(I highly recommend it) and at
the same time I purchased the
TASCON+2 tape so that I can go
back to using my Tasword + 2,
all is well as this is what I'm
using now. However, I would like
to use the MINICHARS Mini1 and
Mini2 (OUTLET 14) in Tasword +2
but can't load them into this
program. I've tried many
addresses but all I get is
rubbish on screen. Can you help
by supplying the address that I
need to load them into?

Finally, keep up the great work
on OUTLET and you'll get no
complaints from me if the price
rises to `5.00. It's still worth
it.

          Many thanks,

        Yours sincerely,

           V. L. Jacks

Brian Cavers to Vincent L.Jacks

Thanks, Vincent.

The address of the Tasword +2
character set is 54528 while
that of Tasword +3 is 38400 and
Tasword 2 is 61184.

Yes, you can program a menu like
the 128K loader menu from BASIC
(and this is valid for SAM too).

There are several stages...

10.PRINT THE OPTIONS ON SCREEN

20.SET A VARIABLE FOR THE TOP
   LINE POSITION, e.g.,if the
   top option on the menu is AT
   5,10 then LET Y=5

30.TEST IF Y IS TOO HIGH OR LOW.

40.PRINT A HIGHLIGHT BAR OVER
   TEXT AT POSITION Y (5 in this
   example). Use OVER 1 to stop
   it erasing the text and use
   either a different PAPER
   colour,BRIGHT 1 or INVERSE 1.
   BRIGHT is a bit dodgy because
   some people use monitors that
   do not show BRIGHT. Anyway,
   here's an example...

  PRINT AT Y,5;OVER 1;INVERSE 1;
  BRIGHT 1;"             "


  There should be enough spaces
  between the quotation marks to
  cover the longest option in
  the menu.

50.WAIT FOR A KEYPRESS, e.g.,
   PAUSE 0: LET K$=INKEY$

60.IF THE KEY FOR "UP" OR "DOWN"
   IS PRESSED THEN YOU NEED TO
   REMOVE THE HIGHLIGHT BAR AND
   CHANGE THE PRINT POSITION
   HIGHER OR LOWER BUT IF IT
   GETS BEYOND THE TOP THEN LINE
   30 CHANGES IT TO THE BOTTOM
   AND VICE-VERSA.

70.IF "ENTER"IS PRESSED("RETURN"
   ON SAM) THEN YOU MUST FIND
   WHICH ROUTINE IS HIGHLIGHTED
   AND GO TO IT.

80.GO BACK TO 50 TO WAIT FOR THE
   NEXT KEYPRESS.

Now I'll give an example...

10 PRINT AT 5,10;"LOAD";AT 6,10;
   "SAVE";AT 7,10;"CAT";AT 8,10;
   "PRINT";AT 9,10;"QUIT"

20 LET Y=5: REM(TOP POSITION)

30 IF Y<5 THEN LET Y=9(see later
35 IF Y>9 THEN LET Y=5( "    "

40 PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;INVERSE
   1;BRIGHT 1;"    "

50 PAUSE 0:LET K$=INKEY$

60 IF K$=CHR$ 11 THEN PRINT AT
   Y,10;OVER 1;"    ":LET Y=Y-1:
   GO TO 30  (CHR$ 11=cursor up)

65 IF K$=CHR$ 10 THEN PRINT AT
   Y,10;OVER 1;"    ":LET Y=Y+1:
   GO TO 30(CHR$ 10=cursor down)

70 IF K$=CHR$ 13 THEN
   GO TO Y*1000:
   REM (CHR$ 13="ENTER")
   (Y*1000 means that it will go
   to line 1000 times the value
   of Y. In this example "LOAD"
   is at the top at position 5
   so Y equals 5 so GOTO Y*1000
   means GOTO 5000 so you would
   put your LOAD routine at 5000

80 GOTO 30 : REM(this is in case
   any other key is pressed it
   will just go back and wait
   for a "proper" keypress.

IF Y<5 at line 30 means "if Y is
smaller than 5" and IF Y>9  at
line 35 means "if Y is greater
than 9". Write again if you have
any problems.          - Brian

From Ted Felstead, WIGAN

Dear Ron/Brian,

Thank you for selecting the past
issues for me. I must say I
think your mag is the best I
have seen for the Spectrum, and
I hope it continues for a long
time yet.

I think it's escaped the notice
of many manufacturers and soft-
ware houses that not everyone
has a PC nor in fact wants one.
I have only been learning comp-
uting for a short time but from
what I have read in mags and on
Micronet it would appear there
is a concerted effort on some
peoples' part to dismiss the
Spectrum as redundant.

I,for one,think Spectrum BASIC's
an extremely friendly language,
especially the syntax-checking,
and is an ideal starter.It would
appear, however, that learning
programming is not a popular
pastime anymore. However keep up
the good work.
               Best Wishes,

               Ted. Felstead

I agree with you, Ted. I am con-
vinced that Spectrum BASIC has
always been underrated by other
than Spectrum BASIC programmers
themselves. String-slicing is
superior to that primitive MID$
of many BASICs, some cannot even
PRINT AT but need a separate
position command. - Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS.

Dear Brian & Ron,

When I saw a brief mention in a
recent Outlet that there was to
be an All Formats Fair here in
Leeds, I thought 'great! I'll go
along and do a review.

However, as I have just about
ceased buying any computer mags,
I found it difficult to discover
just where and when it was being
held. A last-minute phone call
told me so I set off to my first
All Formats Fair. On arrival I
found that the entry price was
`4 which I felt was little short
of outrageous and I dropped the
Fair like a hot potato.

What I'm trying to say is that
possibly many other computer
users missed out simply because
no publicity was given in the
local press, which has a far
wider circulation than any two
or three computer mags put
together. The other point I'd
like to make is that I object to
being asked to pay London prices
for a provincial Fair.

I object even more strongly to
the idea that I should have to
pay an entrance fee of this size
in order to spend my money. I
realise that the organisers have
to make something for their time
and trouble, but if you are
reading this fellas, don't rely
on me to fund your next BMW !!.

In the end I decided to go to a
car boot sale and came home with
an armful of stuff and quite a
bit of change from 4 quid.

If this admission charge carries
on like this, how long will it
be before someone somewhere gets
round to charging an entrance
fee into their shop, store or
super-market etc before we can
buy any of their goods????????

                Malcolm Goodman

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman

The organisers of the fairs get
no direct profit in proportion
to sales so must somehow cover
costs of promotion, advertising,
labour, organisational expenses
etc. that a supermarket can meet
from sales profits. They also
rightly expect to make a profit.
However, I agree `4 is over the
top, especially out of London.`1
would be more acceptable.Perhaps
stallholders could organise the
fair themselves somehow and so
nobody would need to profit from
the actual organizing?

I'll try to remember to put the
price in news items in future.
                         - Brian

From Andy Clapham, NOTTINGHAM


Could you let me know how to
transfer data etc. between my
128 with IF1 and MDV's to the
+3? I assume it is more
complicated than the line of
BASIC in the MDV book and will
require a specific program as
the +3 has a different operating
system I understand.

Do you have any programs or info
on communicating between the
Spectrum and Z88 portable?

           Sincerely,

          Andy Clapham

To Andy Clapham from Brian Gaff

The question really is, what
type of data are we talking
about? Programs are probably
best transferred via tape, as
the +3 has no SAVE/LOAD via its
serial port. Files though, such
as CODE and Tasword files, can
be easily sent over the RS232.

Personally, I would use the two
RS232 ports on the machines
themselves. A recent program in
Add-Enders (iss 44) called
FIDO128 will run on both the
128K and +3, and send files at
1200 baud between machines. I
also have a new program that can
get up to 2400 baud, called
Specterm2.

The cable is probably the
hardest part, as everyone seems
to make printer cables, but not
machine to machine ones. If I
could find a source of open
ended cables, I would be happy
to help.

I do not have a Z88, but the
comments on cables apply equally
here. There were some Z88/Spect-
rum programs in Outlet 41,
Add-Enders. This even included
lead wiring details. I have also
seen some others on BBs, so I
will see if I can download them
for future inclusion in Outlet.

                   - Brian Gaff

From: D. Green, SHEFFIELD

Dear Ron and Brian,

I would be grateful for your
help in a problem I don't seem
to be able to solve. I have a +2
with microdrive and BROTHER
M1109 printer. I can understand
and use all the control codes in
the manual but one - namely the
'DOWNLOAD' feature.

What I am trying to do is to
enable me to define a set of
characters such as the set in
the 'Ansigraphix' program from a
previous issue of OUTLET. I can
define the characters as you do
for U.D.G.s but they never print
out properly.

I think it is to do with the
attribute 'A' which I can't
understand. I would be glad if
you could explain just how to do
this. In case you are not
conversant with this printer I
am enclosing a photostat copy of
the relevant page of the manual.

        Yours sincerely,

            D. Green

Brian Cavers to Mr. D. Green

I have modified FONTWIST to make
an 8-byte character set into an
11-byte set plus the attribute
byte. This modified version,
FONTWIST.2, is in this issue of
OUTLET. Please try it out and
let me know with what success as
I cannot test it myself.

If you want (or need) to explore
the BASIC note that the attri-
bute byte is POKEd in at line
1105 and 3 zeros (for the right
edge of each character) are
POKEd in at line 1500.

The 11 bytes holding the design
for each character are preceded
by a 12th "attribute" byte as
follows...

There are 8 bits in a byte and
each bit (or group of bits) in
the attribute byte represents
proportional spacing or whether
the character will be printed
high or low.There are 9 vertical
pins on a dot-matrix printer so
it is possible to print a
character with a descender or
tail such as j,g,y,p, etc., one
dot further down than the other
characters. This info is held in
the last (highest) bit. This is
the 8th bit as shown in your
manual which numbers them 1 to 8
although it's more common to
number them 0 to 7. I will show
them 1 to 8 here to conform with
your manual. I have set the byte
in FONTWIST to print ALL of the
characters high. Let me know if
you want help adjusting this.

         ATTRIBUTE BYTE

8  1   1=print char high,0=low

7  0   Number of dots from left
6  0   to START character. This
5  0   is normally 0.

4  1   Number of dots from left
3  0   to STOP to give different
2  0   widths, e.g., w will need
1  0   more width than i.

These three groupings of bits
will go together to form a BYTE
thus... 10001000. If you enter,
in BASIC, PRINT BIN 10001000 you
will get 136 printed up and this
is the attribute byte I used. To
calculate different values I'll
list them...

 Decimal   Binary
    0       0000
    1       0001
    2       0010
    3       0011
    4       0100
    5       0101
    6       0110
    7       0111
    8       1000 <-as I used for
    9       1001  8-bit wide set
   10       1010
   11       1011
   12       1100
   13       1101
   14       1110
   15       1111

All characters have 11 bytes but
the remainder is not printed if
using say,8,so the last 3 can be
zeros.

Here's an example,a capital "A":

Attr  11 bytes of
byte  char design
 1    00000000000
 0    00111100000
 0    01000010000
 0    01000010000
 1    01111110000
 0    01000010000
 0    01000010000
 0    00000000000
              !
              these last 3 bytes
              won't be printed &
              the next character
              will start print-
              ing at that pos'n

Fonts designed for the printer
would be much better spaced than
using on-screen fonts of course.

Please give me some feedback on
this because, as I say, I do not
have a printer that accepts such
down-loadable fonts and cannot
test any of this. If you, or
anyone else can confirm it works
or get it to work then it will
be of help to anyone else.

                        - Brian.

From J. Heinrichsons, ANNAN

I wish to join your letters of
complaint about the dis-service
from Garner Designs.

On 8th May I sent them an order
for some items, the cheque was
cashed on 28th May but no goods
have been received.

I wrote three letters about the
non-delivery but they have not
had the courtesy to reply. I
subscribed to the magazine for 6
months but I don't think I will
renew it. Instead, I will write
to their advertisers in the hope
that it will shake them up.

        - J. Heinrichsons

Brian Cavers to J. Heinrichsons

I have asked Daniel Garner to
comment. As stated before,he was
unable to cope with the large
response to the first issue but
the last time he contacted me he
said they would soon be up to
date. However, although I do
sympathise to some extent, with
Garner Design's inability to
meet orders quickly, I find it
unacceptable that any mail order
enterprise should cash a cheque
from a customer knowing that the
goods are not available. SAMCo
did exactly the same to me in
July when I ordered Prince of
Persia (to review!). It still
has not arrived at the time of
writing this (almost November!).

Furthermore, there is nothing
more guaranteed to annoy people
than to ignore letters of
complaint. The least that should
have been done in my view is
that a standard letter or even
postcard should have been
prepared explaining the whole
situation and when goods may be
expected. It would then not be
too labour-intensive to simply
hand-write a name and address.
In addition, an advertisement,
explaining the position would be
appropriate.

We want SAM & SINCLAIR COMPUTING
to succeed so let us hope that
we shall soon be receiving some
letters praising Garner Design's
service.             - Brian

From Peter Brigham, N. YORKS.

Dear Ron and Brian,

May I comment on the subject of
having separate issues for
Spectrum and SAM users?

My opinion is that you should
keep it just as it is, so that
both users can see what's on
offer for each machine. My old
Speccy gave up the ghost some
time ago but it was a great
little machine and brought all
my family and myself lots of fun
and was a pleasure to use. But
the best thing of all is being
able to use Spectrum software
(or most of it) on the Coupe.
                  Peter Brigham

Brian Cavers to Peter Brigham

From last issue we are trying
suggestions from several readers
and are only publishing Spectrum
material in the Spectrum version
and only SAM stuff in the SAM
version IN SO FAR AS POSSIBLE.
However, I note your comments
and, if we get plenty of readers
expressing the same view as
yourself over the next few
months, then we may be persuaded
to return to the way we were.

Meanwhile,if any reader see's an
article or an advert and thinks,
"that's not about my machine,
I'll skip it." Check carefully -
it may have well have parts both
about SAM and Spectrum!
                        - Brian

From: R. Grimmer, WIRRAL

Dear Ron,

I am more than pleased in all
aspects with "Outlet". Please
keep up the good work. May I
enquire if you know how I can
obtain the tape version of 'Lord
of the Rings'(Spectrum Version).

I am not really a games addict,
my reaction is far too slow, but
I have enjoyed the "Hobbit"-type
adventure.

I'd be grateful for any help
that can be offered.

         Yours sincerely,

           R. Grimmer

Brian Cavers to R. Grimmer

The best way is to place an ad
in OUTBOARD or a magazine like
MICRO MART or YOUR SINCLAIR. You
may even get a response from
this letter being published! It
is several years old and not
generally available new.

You might also like THE GOLDEN
COBRA in OUTLET 18. It is not so
complex as THE HOBBIT but it is
very enjoyable if you like text
adventures.

                        - Brian

From: John Cleveland, LONDON

Dear Ron and Brian,

Many congratulations on 50
issues of OUTLET. I've been with
you since the first +3 edition
(No.23) and hope to stay on the
bandwagon for as long as you
keep it rolling. The consistent
high quality and excellent pre-
sentation make each forthcoming
issue something to really look
forward to.

It is especially pleasing still
to find +3-specific utilities,
most recently the magnificent
ULTRA 208. But woe! Kobrahsoft's
DICE, having latterly been
updated to cope with 192 and

203K formats, seems completely
fazed by these 208K wonders, so
we are deprived once more of its
efficient multiple-file copying
on single drive systems.

You told one reader recently you
were thinking of updating
CATLOADER. The biggest single
improvement you could make to
the +3 version would be to
emulate DICE's use of extended
memory for multiple file
copying. Another improvement
would be to display file lengths
(even if there was no room for
the letter "K"). By the way, +3
CATLOADER has one oddity - it
displays spurious filename
extensions when any of the
attributes (protected, system or
archive) is set.

The extra 70K of ULTRA 208 discs
would come in very handy for
CP/M software, but how do you
get CP/M itself to boot from one
of them? I once got MUSIC WRITER
to boot from a 203K disc by
playing around with Brian Gaff's
BOOTLOOK editor, but my attempts
to do the same with CP/M failed.
Any ideas?

I for one would welcome
completely independent Spectrum
and SAM editions of OUTLET,
though I just hope the Spectrum
version won't wither on the
vine. I've got too many 'pooters
already, including a PC
(sorry!!) and I'm definitely not
interested in adding SAM to the
heap.

Having lost countless nights'
sleep getting to grips with the
PC and fathoming the mysteries
of MSDOS, and more recently the
immensely superior DRDOS, I
always find myself coming back
to the +3 where everything is so
much simpler, so much more fun,
and no worries about the hard
disc going down and trashing a
lifetime's collection of files
and there are many things which
are a doddle on the Spectrum
with PCG's DTP software but a
real pain to do on the PC.

So long live the Speccy! - I'll
be faithful to it as long as my
Amstrad hardware holds out,
designer-bugs and all!
              With kind regards,
                 John Cleveland

Brian Cavers to John Cleveland

Many Thanks, John.

Chris Pile can better answer
your CP/M query and I've made a
note to ask him next time I
write (fairly often). He may, of
course, see this and get in
first.Not only has Chris written
the Hi-Format routines but he's
also written a version of CP/M
for SAM so he ought to know if
anyone does!

I'm now trying almost independ-
ant SAM and Spectrum versions of
OUTLET although some letters and
adverts etc. must be in both as
they contain common material by
users with both machines.

I also note what you say about
CATLOADER and if I get a chance
I will at least look at the
feasibility of your ideas. The
use of the ramdisc for temporary
storage while copying several
files with only one drive seems
the most possible.

                       - Brian

From George Wells, THETFORD




Dear Ron & Brian,

I'm getting more able to cope
with this mode of contact now.

I must say at my age: 77, I only
wish something like this was
around when I was younger. The
nearest I can remember, a
computer took up a whole floor
of a building and at the age of
30ish, it was something I never
thought I would be trying to do
today. I am still a bit dim on
these things.

Before the war I was a steeple-
jack and manual worker. Then,
after being knocked about a bit
as a Jap PO, I suffered vertigo,
so my old,loved job was out and
one of my eyes having been used
as an ashtray by the Kempi, I
had to find another occupation.
I became a River Pollution offi-
cer. So,I have certain problems
with this computer interest.


I tried to convert a program to
make OUTLET Nos. 26, 36, 35,
print out like they do on 48 and
49. I don't know, I just kept
making a balls-up of it. Do you
have a merge program to do it?
or do you intend to issue one in
the future?

Sorry to be such an idiot, but
THERE YOU GO! Better not worry
you further. Thanks and Good
Luck.
              - George C. Wells





Thanks,George. I assume you mean
the TABLOID option? Just load a
recent issue until the CONTENTS
appears and then put in the old
OUTLET disc before you select.
You may need to look through one
or two issues if your selection
is not in every issue such as
CHECKOUT or DRIVECHAT.

                       - Brian.

Thanks, Vincent.

The address of the Tasword +2 character set is 54528 while that of Tasword +3 is 38400 and Tasword 2 is 61184.

Yes, you can program a menu like the 128K loader menu from BASIC (and this is valid for SAM too).

There are several stages...

10.PRINT THE OPTIONS ON SCREEN

20.SET A VARIABLE FOR THE TOP LINE POSITION, e.g.,if the top option on the menu is AT 5,10 then LET Y=5

30.TEST IF Y IS TOO HIGH OR LOW.

40.PRINT A HIGHLIGHT BAR OVER TEXT AT POSITION Y (5 in this example). Use OVER 1 to stop it erasing the text and use either a different PAPER colour,BRIGHT 1 or INVERSE 1. BRIGHT is a bit dodgy because some people use monitors that do not show BRIGHT. Anyway, here's an example...

PRINT AT Y,5;OVER 1;INVERSE 1; BRIGHT 1;"             "

There should be enough spaces between the quotation marks to cover the longest option in the menu.

50.WAIT FOR A KEYPRESS, e.g., PAUSE 0: LET K$=INKEY$

60.IF THE KEY FOR "UP" OR "DOWN" IS PRESSED THEN YOU NEED TO REMOVE THE HIGHLIGHT BAR AND CHANGE THE PRINT POSITION HIGHER OR LOWER BUT IF IT GETS BEYOND THE TOP THEN LINE 30 CHANGES IT TO THE BOTTOM AND VICE-VERSA.

70.IF "ENTER"IS PRESSED("RETURN" ON SAM) THEN YOU MUST FIND WHICH ROUTINE IS HIGHLIGHTED AND GO TO IT.

80.GO BACK TO 50 TO WAIT FOR THE NEXT KEYPRESS.

Now I'll give an example...

10 PRINT AT 5,10;"LOAD";AT 6,10; "SAVE";AT 7,10;"CAT";AT 8,10; "PRINT";AT 9,10;"QUIT"

20 LET Y=5: REM(TOP POSITION)

30 IF Y<5 THEN LET Y=9(see later 35 IF Y>9 THEN LET Y=5( "    "

40 PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;INVERSE 1;BRIGHT 1;"    "

50 PAUSE 0:LET K$=INKEY$

60 IF K$=CHR$ 11 THEN PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;"    ":LET Y=Y-1: GO TO 30  (CHR$ 11=cursor up)

65 IF K$=CHR$ 10 THEN PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;"    ":LET Y=Y+1: GO TO 30(CHR$ 10=cursor down)

70 IF K$=CHR$ 13 THEN GO TO Y*1000: REM (CHR$ 13="ENTER") (Y*1000 means that it will go to line 1000 times the value of Y. In this example "LOAD" is at the top at position 5 so Y equals 5 so GOTO Y*1000 means GOTO 5000 so you would put your LOAD routine at 5000

80 GOTO 30 : REM(this is in case any other key is pressed it will just go back and wait for a "proper" keypress.

IF Y<5 at line 30 means "if Y is smaller than 5" and IF Y>9  at line 35 means "if Y is greater than 9". Write again if you have any problems.          - Brian

Brian Cavers to Mr. D. Green

I have modified FONTWIST to make an 8-byte character set into an 11-byte set plus the attribute byte. This modified version, FONTWIST.2, is in this issue of OUTLET. Please try it out and let me know with what success as I cannot test it myself.

If you want (or need) to explore the BASIC note that the attri- bute byte is POKEd in at line 1105 and 3 zeros (for the right edge of each character) are POKEd in at line 1500.

The 11 bytes holding the design for each character are preceded by a 12th "attribute" byte as follows...

There are 8 bits in a byte and each bit (or group of bits) in the attribute byte represents proportional spacing or whether the character will be printed high or low.There are 9 vertical pins on a dot-matrix printer so it is possible to print a character with a descender or tail such as j,g,y,p, etc., one dot further down than the other characters. This info is held in the last (highest) bit. This is the 8th bit as shown in your manual which numbers them 1 to 8 although it's more common to number them 0 to 7. I will show them 1 to 8 here to conform with your manual. I have set the byte in FONTWIST to print ALL of the characters high. Let me know if you want help adjusting this.

ATTRIBUTE BYTE

8  1   1=print char high,0=low

7  0   Number of dots from left 6  0   to START character. This 5  0   is normally 0.

4  1   Number of dots from left 3  0   to STOP to give different 2  0   widths, e.g., w will need 1  0   more width than i.

These three groupings of bits will go together to form a BYTE thus... 10001000. If you enter, in BASIC, PRINT BIN 10001000 you will get 136 printed up and this is the attribute byte I used. To calculate different values I'll list them...

Decimal   Binary

```text
    0       0000
    1       0001
    2       0010
    3       0011
    4       0100
    5       0101
    6       0110
    7       0111
```

8       1000 <-as I used for 9       1001  8-bit wide set

```text
   10       1010
   11       1011
   12       1100
   13       1101
   14       1110
   15       1111
```

All characters have 11 bytes but the remainder is not printed if using say,8,so the last 3 can be zeros.

Here's an example,a capital "A":

Attr  11 bytes of byte  char design

```text
 1    00000000000
 0    00111100000
 0    01000010000
 0    01000010000
 1    01111110000
 0    01000010000
 0    01000010000
 0    00000000000
              !
```

these last 3 bytes won't be printed & the next character will start print- ing at that pos'n

Fonts designed for the printer would be much better spaced than using on-screen fonts of course.

Please give me some feedback on this because, as I say, I do not have a printer that accepts such down-loadable fonts and cannot test any of this. If you, or anyone else can confirm it works or get it to work then it will be of help to anyone else.

Да, меню наподобие загрузчика 128K можно запрограммировать на BASIC (и этот способ сгодится и для SAM).

Здесь есть несколько этапов...

10. НАПЕЧАТАТЬ ПУНКТЫ МЕНЮ НА ЭКРАНЕ

20. ЗАДАТЬ ПЕРЕМЕННУЮ ДЛЯ ПОЗИЦИИ ВЕРХНЕЙ СТРОКИ, например, если верхний пункт меню находится в позиции AT 5,10, то LET Y=5

30. ПРОВЕРИТЬ, НЕ СТАЛО ЛИ ЗНАЧЕНИЕ Y СЛИШКОМ ВЫСОКИМ ИЛИ НИЗКИМ.

40. НАПЕЧАТАТЬ ВЫДЕЛЯЮЩУЮ ПОЛОСУ ПОВЕРХ ТЕКСТА В ПОЗИЦИИ Y (в этом примере — 5). Используйте OVER 1, чтобы полоса не затирала текст, а также либо другой цвет PAPER, либо BRIGHT 1, либо INVERSE 1. С BRIGHT есть небольшая загвоздка, поскольку некоторые используют мониторы, не отображающие повышенную яркость. В любом случае, вот пример...

```text
PRINT AT Y,5;OVER 1;INVERSE 1;BRIGHT 1;"             "
```

Между кавычками должно быть достаточно пробелов, чтобы перекрыть самый длинный пункт меню.

50. ОЖИДАТЬ НАЖАТИЯ КЛАВИШИ, например: `PAUSE 0: LET K$=INKEY$`

60. ЕСЛИ НАЖАТА КЛАВИША «ВВЕРХ» ИЛИ «ВНИЗ», ВАМ НУЖНО СТЕРЕТЬ ВЫДЕЛЯЮЩУЮ ПОЛОСУ И ИЗМЕНИТЬ ПОЗИЦИЮ ПЕЧАТИ ВЫШЕ ИЛИ НИЖЕ; ЕСЛИ ЖЕ ОНА ВЫХОДИТ ЗА ПРЕДЕЛЫ ВЕРХНЕЙ ГРАНИЦЫ, ТО СТРОКА 30 ПЕРЕМЕЩАЕТ ЕЕ В САМЫЙ НИЗ, И НАОБОРОТ.

70. ЕСЛИ НАЖАТ «ENTER» («RETURN» НА SAM), ВЫ ДОЛЖНЫ ОПРЕДЕЛИТЬ, КАКОЙ ПУНКТ СЕЙЧАС ВЫДЕЛЕН, И ПЕРЕЙТИ К НЕМУ.

80. ВЕРНУТЬСЯ К ПУНКТУ 50 В ОЖИДАНИИ СЛЕДУЮЩЕГО НАЖАТИЯ КЛАВИШИ.

А теперь приведу пример...

```text
10 PRINT AT 5,10;"LOAD";AT 6,10;"SAVE";AT 7,10;"CAT";AT 8,10;"PRINT";AT 9,10;"QUIT"
20 LET Y=5: REM (ВЕРХНЯЯ ПОЗИЦИЯ)
30 IF Y<5 THEN LET Y=9
35 IF Y>9 THEN LET Y=5
40 PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;INVERSE 1;BRIGHT 1;"     "
50 PAUSE 0: LET K$=INKEY$
60 IF K$=CHR$ 11 THEN PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;"     ": LET Y=Y-1: GO TO 30: REM (CHR$ 11 = курсор вверх)
65 IF K$=CHR$ 10 THEN PRINT AT Y,10;OVER 1;"     ": LET Y=Y+1: GO TO 30: REM (CHR$ 10 = курсор вниз)
70 IF K$=CHR$ 13 THEN GO TO Y*1000: REM (CHR$ 13 = "ENTER")
   REM (Y*1000 означает переход на строку, номер которой в 1000 раз больше значения Y.
   REM В этом примере "LOAD" находится на самом верху в позиции 5,
   REM значит Y равен 5, и GOTO Y*1000 означает GOTO 5000,
   REM то есть вашу подпрограмму LOAD следует разместить со строки 5000)
80 GOTO 30: REM (это на случай нажатия любой другой клавиши,
   REM программа просто вернется назад и будет ждать "правильного" нажатия)
```

`IF Y<5` в строке 30 означает «если Y меньше 5», а `IF Y>9` в строке 35 означает «если Y больше 9». Пишите снова, если возникнут трудности.

— Brian

Brian Cavers мистеру D. Green:

Я модифицировал FONTWIST, чтобы превратить 8-байтный набор символов в 11-байтный плюс байт атрибута. Эта доработанная версия, FONTWIST.2, вошла в текущий выпуск OUTLET. Пожалуйста, опробуйте её и дайте знать о результатах, так как сам я протестировать её не могу.

Если вы захотите (или вам понадобится) изучить BASIC-код, обратите внимание: байт атрибута заносится через POKE в строке 1105, а 3 нуля (для правого края каждого символа) заносятся через POKE в строке 1500.

11 байтам, содержащим рисунок каждого символа, предшествует 12-й «атрибутный» байт следующего формата...

В байте 8 бит, и каждый бит (или группа битов) в атрибутном байте отвечает за пропорциональный интервал либо указывает, будет ли символ печататься высоко или низко. У матричного принтера 9 вертикальных иголок, поэтому символы с нижними выносными элементами («хвостами»), такие как j, g, y, p и т. д., можно печатать на одну точку ниже остальных. Эта информация хранится в последнем (старшем) бите. В вашем руководстве это 8-й бит (там биты нумеруются от 1 до 8, хотя чаще принято считать от 0 до 7). Для соответствия вашей инструкции я буду использовать нумерацию от 1 до 8. В FONTWIST я настроил этот байт так, чтобы ВСЕ символы печатались в верхнем положении. Сообщите, если потребуется помощь с его изменением.

```text
         БАЙТ АТРИБУТА

8  1   1=печатать символ высоко, 0=низко

7  0   Количество точек слева
6  0   до НАЧАЛА символа. Обычно
5  0   равно 0.

4  1   Количество точек слева
3  0   до КОНЦА символа для разной
2  0   ширины: например, для «w»
1  0   нужно больше места, чем для «i».
```

Эти три группы битов объединяются в БАЙТ, вот так: `10001000`. Если вы введете в BASIC команду `PRINT BIN 10001000`, то на экране появится число 136 — именно такой атрибутный байт я и использовал. Чтобы рассчитывать другие значения, приведу таблицу:

```text
 Десятич.  Двоичн.
    0       0000
    1       0001
    2       0010
    3       0011
    4       0100
    5       0101
    6       0110
    7       0111
    8       1000 <- использовано мной
    9       1001    для 8-битного набора
   10       1010
   11       1011
   12       1100
   13       1101
   14       1110
   15       1111
```

Все символы задаются 11 байтами, но остаток не печатается, если задано, скажем, 8 — поэтому последние 3 байта могут быть нулями.

Вот пример, заглавная буква «A»:

```text
Байт    11 байт
атриб.  рисунка символа
 1      00000000000
 0      00111100000
 0      01000010000
 0      01000010000
 1      01111110000
 0      01000010000
 0      01000010000
 0      00000000000
                !
                эти последние 3 байта
                печататься не будут, и
                следующий символ начнет
                печать с этой позиции
```

Шрифты, созданные специально для принтера, естественно, имели бы гораздо более аккуратные интервалы, чем перенесенные с экрана.

Пожалуйста, напишите о результатах, поскольку, повторюсь, у меня нет принтера с поддержкой загружаемых шрифтов, и проверить всё это я сам не в состоянии. Если вы или кто-то ещё подтвердите работоспособность или доведете всё до ума, это поможет и остальным.

— Brian.
